answer: Thank you for reaching out to us about the SAML login issue. We recommend comparing the assertion consumer service URL in your identity provider against the value shown on the SSO settings page. They must match exactly, including the trailing path. Additionally, please confirm that the NameID in a failing assertion is the user's email address in lower case. If new users should be created on first login, enable just-in-time provisioning and set a default role for provisioned users. Finally, ensure that at least one administrator account has password access while testing, so a misconfiguration does not lock the whole organisation out. Please let us know what you observed after trying these steps.

We appreciate your question about the expected delay in metrics arriving at your monitoring system. According to our documentation, you can expect a delay of up to two minutes on metrics since they are aggregated before being sent [DOC-INT-002]. This is a normal behavior for our service. To confirm, you can check the forwarding status page, which shows the last successful delivery and any error returned by the destination [DOC-INT-002]. If you have any further questions or concerns, please let us know what you observed.

Thanks for reaching out. We'll need to investigate further to determine the cause of the issue. According to our documentation, common causes of environment variables and secrets not being read include the variable being set at project scope but read at service scope, the application logging its configuration at startup, and an environment override existing that is not visible on the main settings page [DOC-DEPLOY-004 | Common causes | All compute services]. We recommend checking the scope at which the variable was defined, storing sensitive values as secrets rather than variables, reviewing the environment overrides page, and redeploying after changing configuration [DOC-DEPLOY-004 | Resolution | All compute services]. A support engineer will look at this ticket to assist you further.

Thanks for reaching out. To store sensitive information as secrets, you should reference them from the environment rather than committing them. This way, they are masked in logs and not readable through the API. You can check the environment overrides page to see values that differ from the defaults for each environment. If you've made changes to your configuration, be sure to redeploy after updating your settings. This will ensure that running containers pick up the new values without a restart. Please let us know what you observe after making these changes.

Thanks for reaching out. We'd like to help you troubleshoot the elevated response latency. According to our documentation, a large gap between median and 95th percentile latency on the metrics page may indicate contention or queueing [DOC-PERF-001]. We recommend checking memory utilisation across instances, as sustained utilisation above eighty per cent can show up as latency before failure [DOC-PERF-001]. Additionally, reviewing the dependency timing breakdown on the trace view may help identify whether the time is being spent in your service or waiting on another [DOC-PERF-001].

To revert to an earlier revision, you can follow the documented steps. According to our knowledge base, you can open the revisions page for the service and identify the last revision that was healthy. Then, select roll back on that revision. This will move traffic to the previous revision within roughly thirty seconds without rebuilding the service. If the release included a database migration, it's recommended to roll the migration back before the service to avoid schema issues. Please record the incident and the reason for the rollback before deploying a fix, while the detail is still fresh. You can then observe the results of this process and let us know what you see.

Thank you for reaching out to us about the issue with your database restore taking hours. Database connection pool exhaustion can cause errors indicating no connection is available, and this can be caused by the pool size multiplied by the instance count exceeding the database connection limit [DOC-PERF-003]. It can also be caused by connections not being returned to the pool after use or long-running transactions holding connections open [DOC-PERF-003]. To troubleshoot this issue, we recommend verifying that the database connection limit has not been exceeded and checking for any long-running transactions or connections not being returned to the pool. Please let us know what you observe after checking these potential causes.

Thank you for reaching out about hitting the rate limit unexpectedly. The rate limit applies per organisation, not per key, so having multiple keys does not increase the available quota [DOC-API-001 | Notes | All plans]. To better understand the rate limit, please read the rate limit headers returned with every response, which give the limit, the remaining allowance and the reset time [DOC-API-001 | Resolution | All plans]. If you're still experiencing issues, please let us know what you observed.
Thank you for getting in touch. I could not find documentation that answers this, so a support engineer will look at your ticket and reply directly.

Thanks for reaching out about your billing concerns. The billing period for your CloudServe account runs from the anniversary of the subscription date. To understand your invoice and usage breakdown, please open the usage breakdown for the period, which itemises charges by service and by environment. This will help you identify resources in staging or development environments, which are billed at the same rate as production. Additionally, check the billing period dates at the top of the invoice to ensure they align with your expectations.

Thank you for reaching out to us about the unexpected overage charges. To change the behavior so that your service is not stopped when the spend cap is reached, you should configure alerts at fifty, eighty and ninety-five per cent of your plan allowance rather than relying on the cap as a warning. Additionally, you can deliberately decide between a hard spend cap, which stops the service, and overage, which continues at the listed rate. For production workloads, overage is generally the preferred option. Please check the current period usage against the plan allowance on the billing page and decide which option is best for your service.

Thanks for reaching out. We can help you with exporting audit logs. On our Business plan, audit logs are retained for ninety days [DOC-SEC-001]. To export the relevant period, you can filter the audit log by actor, resource, and date range [DOC-SEC-003]. You can then export the relevant period to object storage for anything needed beyond the retention window. Exports are not subject to retention limits. Note that read access to resources is not logged on our Business plan, only administrative and configuration changes are logged. We recommend configuring continuous export to your own storage if a policy requires retention longer than the plan provides. Please let us know what you observed when you try these steps.

Thanks for reaching out. We've identified that the symptoms you're experiencing are consistent with issues related to webhook delivery, retries, and signature verification. According to our documentation, common causes of these issues include a non-2xx status returned by the endpoint, slow response times, and incorrect signature computation. To resolve the issue, we recommend checking the webhook delivery log, which records every attempt with the response status and body for the last seven days. Additionally, we suggest returning 2xx as quickly as possible and processing the event asynchronously. It's also essential to compute the signature over the raw request body before any parsing, and to make your handler idempotent using the event identifier.

Thank you for reaching out about the SAML login issue. Based on the information provided, it's possible that the assertion consumer service URL in your identity provider does not match the value shown on the SSO settings page, or that just-in-time provisioning is disabled on the connection. To troubleshoot this issue, please compare the assertion consumer service URL in your identity provider against the value shown on the SSO settings page. They must match exactly, including the trailing path. Additionally, confirm that just-in-time provisioning is enabled and that a default role is set for provisioned users. If you have any further questions or observations, please reply to this ticket.

Thanks for reaching out. We retain audit logs for ninety days on Business plans [DOC-SEC-001]. To access the relevant period, you can filter the audit log by actor, resource, and date range [DOC-SEC-003]. You can then export the relevant period to object storage for anything needed beyond the retention window. Exports are not subject to retention limits. Note that read access to resources is not logged on Business plans, only administrative and configuration changes are recorded. Please let us know what you observed after attempting these steps.

Thank you for reaching out to us about the issue with your developer not being able to access a project. This can be caused by the role being granted at project scope rather than organisation scope [DOC-ACCT-001 | Common causes | All plans]. To resolve this, you can check the effective permissions view for the user, which resolves direct roles and group memberships together [DOC-ACCT-001 | Resolution | All plans]. Please confirm that the invitation was accepted and that the user has the correct permissions. If you have any further questions or observations, please reply to this ticket.

Thank you for reaching out to us about the issue with log forwarding to your external system. According to our documentation, forwarding pauses after one hour of consecutive failures and must be resumed manually once the destination is healthy [DOC-INT-002]. To troubleshoot this issue, we recommend checking the forwarding status page, which shows the last successful delivery and any error returned by the destination [DOC-INT-002]. Additionally, you may want to verify the destination credential separately if delivery has stopped entirely, as expired credentials are the most common cause [DOC-INT-002]. Please let us know what you observed after checking these steps.

Thank you for reaching out to CloudServe support. According to our documentation, the billing period runs from the anniversary of the subscription date [DOC-BILL-001]. This means that the period may not align with the calendar month. To better understand your invoice and usage breakdown, we recommend checking the billing period dates at the top of the invoice [DOC-BILL-001]. If you have any further questions or concerns, please do not hesitate to reply.

Thank you for reaching out about the increased response times. Elevated response latency can be caused by several factors, including contention or queueing, high memory utilisation, or dependencies on other services. To diagnose the issue, we recommend comparing the median and 95th percentile latency on the metrics page, checking memory utilisation across instances, and reviewing the dependency timing breakdown on the trace view. If load is predictable, adjusting the autoscaling policy may also help. Cold starts can also affect the first request to a new instance, so frequent scaling events may raise the 95th percentile even when the service itself is healthy.

Thank you for reaching out about your production workload being stopped due to a spend cap. According to our documentation, spend caps apply per organisation and cannot currently be set per project [DOC-BILL-003]. To resolve this issue, you can raise the cap immediately from the billing page, and the service should resume within a minute [DOC-BILL-003]. Please check the billing page to see the current period usage against the plan allowance and decide whether to configure a hard spend cap or overage [DOC-BILL-003].
